speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and now have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, can you tell me if the knee pain comes on suddenly, typically at night, and if you have noticed any redness or warmth in either joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome).

The clinical picture of a history of inflammatory arthritis (left ankle), current monoarthritis (right knee), and urethritis, combined with recent new sexual partners, is classic for reactive arthritis. I need to confirm the onset of the knee swelling to rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Uric acid. REQUEST IMAGES: Right knee X-ray.
